episodes.177633: Rapidly melting snow from an above normal snowpack caused flooding along numerous streams and at many river forecast points in the Milk River Watershed.
episodes.177819: Above normal temperatures accelerated snowmelt from a near-record snowpack. This  resulted in high and fast flows on several rivers and drainages across Western Colorado. The increased runoff and flooding compromised several county roads and bridges across Montezuma, Archuleta, Routt, Delta, Dolores, Montrose, and Moffat counties.
episodes.177842: Thunderstorms pushing offshore from the Brevard and Treasure Coasts produced strong wind gusts. While storms along the Volusia County coast produced small hail.
episodes.179015: A strong cold front moved through the area during the April 13-15 timeframe, bring with it a round of strong thunderstorms with numerous gusts in excess of 34 knots along the coast.
episodes.179136: Rapid snowmelt from a few day period of well above normal temperatures focused on the 11-13th of April resulted in minor to locally moderate flooding through much of the Big Sioux River Basin. Some areas north of I-90 lost between 2 to 5 inches of snow water equivalent (SWE) from the first to second week of April, but antecedent drought conditions resulted in only a percentage of this water actually making it into the river system.
episodes.179261: A warm front extended east across NE FL from a surface low in the NE Gulf of Mexico during the morning. By the afternoon, the warm front was lifting northward across SE GA. Strong to severe storms formed near the warm front across SE GA in the afternoon and then along the sea breeze merger across NE FL in the afternoon and evening over a moist and unstable airmass.
episodes.179262: A warm front extended east across NE FL from a surface low in the NE Gulf of Mexico during the morning. By the afternoon, the warm front was lifting northward across SE GA. Strong to severe storms formed near the warm front across SE GA in the afternoon and then along the sea breeze merger across NE FL in the afternoon and evening over a moist and unstable airmass.
episodes.179316: The Mustinka River and its tributaries experienced flooding due to the rapid snowmelt in western Minnesota caused by frozen soils and a quick thaw in the second week of April. The area, including Wheaton, saw a significant snow depth of 32 inches on April 6th. As a result, a large amount of snowmelt flowed into the waterways, leading to numerous county and township roads being submerged. To safeguard properties, many communities initiated sandbagging operations.
episodes.179460: A cluster of fast moving, weak showers in the afternoon of the 13th created high winds as they collapsed. Winds not associated with the showers were gusting to around 30-40 mph and as the showers collapsed, short-lived gusts reached up to 65 mph in southwestern Nebraska. A barn's roof was torn off from one of these wind gusts. Blowing dust was also reported with these wind reports with visibility being reduced down to near zero for about 20 minutes.
episodes.179461: A cluster of fast moving, weak showers, and a couple of storms, in the afternoon of the 13th created high winds as they collapsed. Winds not associated with the showers were gusting to around 30-40 mph and as the showers collapsed, short-lived gusts reached up to 64 mph in Northwestern Kansas. A small dormant tree was blown over from one of the gusts.
episodes.179586: Rapid melting of much above normal snowpack caused widespread, and at times, extensive flooding over portions of west and central Upper Michigan from the 12th into the 25th.  Extensive impacts from the flooding caused Governor Whitmer to declare a state of emergency declaration for eight counties in west and central Upper Michigan on the 21st.
episodes.179765: A cold front initiated highly elevated showers and embedded thunderstorms during the late afternoon hours of April 14th. As this activity transitioned east, it produced strong gusty winds as high as 70 MPH. In addition to gusty winds, dry lightning was also reported along with some blowing dust.
episodes.179780: A nearly stationary front began to move slowly northward across South Florida on April 12th, focusing deep moisture over the region. An mid to upper level low pressure over the NW Gulf of Mexico and an upper level jet stream over the eastern Gulf of Mexico contributed to providing the necessary atmospheric forcing for areas of persistent heavy rain and strong thunderstorms across most of SE Florida.
episodes.179791: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced high winds.
episodes.179793: Strong thunderstorms moved over the marine area and produced strong winds gusts.
episodes.179839: A few storms moved through far western Kansas in the early evening across far western Kansas.
episodes.179842: A line of thunderstorms formed in the western combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles during the afternoon of the 13th. A few of these storms within the line produced some wind gusts in excess of 58 mph.
episodes.179862: A surface low moving northward out of the Gulf brought scattered thunderstorms across Central and South Central GA. CAPE values reached into the 500 to 1000 J/Kg range with SRH values of 100-200 m2/s2. The SPC upgraded the severe outlook to a Slight risk in a line from Harris County to Wheeler county while areas south of I20 and north of a line from Troup to Laurens county remained in a Marginal risk. The anticipated threats included damaging winds and a tornado or two.
episodes.179892: A line of thunderstorms moved across the area and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.179942: Snowmelt brought enhanced flows, with avalanches, flooding and debris flows.
episodes.179965: A low pressure area over the northern Gulf of Mexico and a warm front across South Florida led to the formation of strong thunderstorms over parts of South Florida during the afternoon hours.
episodes.180055: Snowmelt flooding along the Minnesota Tributaries began in mid-April, with a few locations persisting into early May.

events.narrative: The Milk River at Dodson (DMRM8) rose above its flood stage of 23 feet at 5:45 PM on April 12th.  The river then crested at 23.47 feet at 7:15PM on April 12th.  The river would go below flood stage at 8:30 PM on April 12th before rising back above flood stage at 3:00 PM on April 14th.  The river would fall below flood stage at 4:20 PM on April 14th.

A small tornado began in Dania Beach on NE 6th Court just south of Ft. Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport, causing mainly fence and tree damage to the surrounding neighborhood. The tornado skipped as the parent storm moved WNW across Federal Highway, with the next area of tornado damage noted at a church on NW 5th Avenue and 3rd Terrace where the west edge of the roof peeled and blew off to the east, and the front door facing north was blown in. Extensive tree damage was noted westward along Old Griffin Road next to the Dania Cut-Off Canal, then damaged at least half a dozen mobile homes in the Ocean Waterway community west of Bryan Road and east of I-95. The mobile home damage was in the form of peeled roofs, metal siding torn off, and damaged power poles. ||The tornado was rated on the high end of the EF-0 scale based primarily on damage in the mobile home park. A tornadic debris signature (TDS) was also noted on radar with this tornado. Damage totals are estimates.

The Milk River at Nashua (NSHM8) rose above its flood stage of 20 feet at 9:50 PM on April 12th. The river then crested at 26.47 feet at 11:00 AM on April 18th. The river would fall below flood stage at 9:40 AM on April 25th.

Michigan DOT closed Highway M-28 at Ewen due to snowmelt flooding over the bridge along the South Branch of the Ontonagon River from the 13th until the 18th.  Traffic was detoured via US-2 and US-45. Ontonagon County was added to the state emergency declaration by Governor Whitmer on the 21st to assist in flood recovery efforts.

Michigan DOT reported snowmelt flood water over US Highway 41 between 27.75 and US Highway 2 near Rapid River on the 13th.  Flooding was also reported along the Sturgeon River near Nahma Junction from the 15th through the 23rd.

Rapid snowmelt resulted in Dry Creek, which runs underneath Highway 40, coming out of its banks. As a result, Highway 40 was closed and shut down in both directions from Craig to Steamboat Springs due to safety concerns. Schools in Hayden were closed. Flood waters did not recede for several days.

Secondary roads were impacted by flooding along the Paint River, Iron River and other tributaries across the county.  Iron County was included in a state of emergency declaration by Governor Whitmer on 4/21 to aid in flood recovery efforts.

Flooding along the Michigamme River including secondary roads and property constituted much of the flood impacts in April for Dickinson County.  County Road 577 in Vulcan was also closed from the 15th into the 17th due to high water.  Governor Whitmer declared a state of emergency for Dickinson County on the 21st to open up state funds to assist in flood recovery efforts.
